questions.skill: Definition of a translation
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Points A and B are different. Write a precise definition of the translation that maps A to B.
questions.prompt_markup: Points A and B are different. Write a precise definition of the translation that maps A to B.
questions.correct_answer: It maps each point P to the point P′ such that PP′ has the same length as AB, is parallel to AB (or on line AB), and points in the same direction.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: same length, parallel (or collinear), same direction. Accept "ABP′P is a parallelogram" for points P not on line AB.

sections.skill: Prove from the definition that translations keep lengths

branch.new_demand: Prove from the definition that a translation preserves length, including the case on one line.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the parallel, equal segments used there are the facts the proof uses.

questions.skill: Prove from the definition that translations keep lengths
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A translation maps P to P′ and Q to Q′, where Q is not on line PP′. Prove that PQ = P′Q′.
questions.prompt_markup: A translation maps P to P′ and Q to Q′, where Q is not on line PP′. Prove that PQ = P′Q′.
questions.required_method: Use the definition (PP′ and QQ′ are parallel, the same length, and the same direction) to show PP′Q′Q is a parallelogram.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: PP′ ∥ QQ′ and PP′ = QQ′ in the same direction, so PP′Q′Q is a parallelogram (one pair of opposite sides parallel and congruent); opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent, so PQ = P′Q′. Invalid: assuming translations preserve length.
questions.set_target: Define a translation precisely using parallel segments of equal length and direction, and use the definition to locate images
questions.target_skill: Prove from the definition that translations keep lengths

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that T(x, y) = (x + a, y + b) maps every nonvertical line y = mx + k to a line with the same slope m (so the image is parallel to the line or is the line itself).
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that T(x, y) = (x + a, y + b) maps every nonvertical line y = mx + k to a line with the same slope m (so the image is parallel to the line or is the line itself).
questions.correct_answer: The image of (x, mx + k) is (X, Y) = (x + a, mx + k + b), and Y = m(X - a) + k + b = mX + (k + b - ma): slope m.
questions.required_method: Take any point (x, mx + k), find its image, and show the image satisfies an equation with slope m.
questions.grading_note: Any valid algebraic proof. Essential: general point; image; substitution x = X - a; slope m; same line exactly when b = ma. Invalid: checking one example line.
